items.title: Opposition presses Housing Minister David Lee to step aside after High Court ruling in fraud case
items.summary: The opposition PNM has intensified calls for Housing Minister David Lee to leave his portfolio while criminal proceedings against him continue. Leader of Government Business Barry Padarath responded to the demand.

items.title: Nigel Baptiste retiring as head of Republic Financial Holdings and Republic Bank
items.summary: Nigel Baptiste is retiring as group president and CEO of Republic Financial Holdings Ltd and as president and managing director of Republic Bank Ltd, ending a career of more than three decades at the institution.

items.title: Foreign Minister Sobers says Trinidad and Tobago will not leave the Commonwealth
items.summary: Foreign and Caricom Affairs Minister Sean Sobers said the government has no intention of withdrawing from the Commonwealth despite Britain's position on reparations for slavery.

items.title: T&T prepares for Concacaf Gold Cup play-in against Antigua & Barbuda
items.summary: USA-based winger Kaihim Thomas says he is available for Trinidad and Tobago's Gold Cup play-in matches against Antigua & Barbuda on November 12 and 16.

items.title: Cabinet approves new board for South-West Regional Health Authority
items.summary: Health Minister Dr Lackram Bodoe said Cabinet has approved a new board for the SWRHA, with the appointments expected to be formalised soon.

items.title: Transparency Institute says procurement amendments weaken public spending safeguards
items.summary: The Trinidad and Tobago Transparency Institute says recent legislative amendments have weakened public procurement safeguards, leaving billions of dollars in state spending under reduced oversight.

items.title: GrowSF-backed candidates sweep San Francisco school board races
items.summary: Candidates backed by moderate group GrowSF won three school board seats, and for the first time in over a decade no teachers-union-backed candidate won. Tim Tung and Autumn Brown Garibay took the final two seats.

items.title: California's Great America to close permanently in 2027
items.summary: The Santa Clara amusement park, a longtime Bay Area landmark, will close for good in 2027.

items.title: Fremont woman charged with assaulting East Bay council member
items.summary: The Alameda County District Attorney has charged a Fremont woman in an alleged assault on an East Bay council member on October 25.

items.title: Analyst questions PM's 'Yellow is the Code' message to Grenada's new prime minister
items.summary: A regional political analyst criticised Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar's use of the slogan in her congratulations to Grenada's NDC after its landslide election victory.

items.title: Jane Kim declares victory in California insurance commissioner race as results firm up
items.summary: Jane Kim has declared victory over state Sen. Ben Allen, though the AP has not called the race. Governor-elect Xavier Becerra held his first press conference but gave few details of his agenda.

items.title: SFPD serves search warrant at Sea Cliff house tied to alleged squatting
items.summary: San Francisco police executed a search warrant at a $4 million Sea Cliff home at the center of alleged squatting activity.

items.title: Google, Meta and TikTok sue to block California law on addictive social media features for kids
items.summary: AB 1709, set to take effect January 1, bars features such as personalized recommendations and autoplay for users under 16. The companies argue in federal court that it violates the First Amendment.

items.title: Libghostty 1.0 released
items.summary: Version 1.0 of libghostty, the embeddable terminal library from the Ghostty project, has been released.

items.title: Man recovers from knife wound through eye and brain
items.summary: Doctors say the exact path of the wound, rather than its apparent severity, determined the patient's unexpected recovery.

items.title: Outbound SIP calling made available to all organizations
items.summary: A platform has opened outbound SIP calling to all organizations.

items.title: Sodium-ion batteries near cost parity with LFP
items.summary: Sodium-ion battery costs are approaching those of lithium iron phosphate batteries.

items.title: Ships loiter near subsea cables after Iran threatens attacks
items.summary: Iran threatened to attack subsea cables if the US escalates military strikes, and ships have been observed lingering near cable routes.

items.title: Trinidad and Tobago advances Kigali Amendment controls on HFCs
items.summary: Trinidad and Tobago and Uganda have advanced controls on hydrofluorocarbons under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol.

items.title: Mayor Lurie to direct $12 million to Mission District
items.summary: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie will direct $12 million toward addressing conditions in the Mission District.

items.title: Wing Commander and Ultima re-releases arrive on Steam and GOG
items.summary: EA has re-released classic Wing Commander and Ultima titles on Steam and GOG.

items.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production
items.summary: Elon Musk signalled the end of the Cybertruck to free up production for Cybercabs, Tesla's driverless autonomous taxis.

items.title: Valkyries championship parade draws crowds that strained Muni and BART
items.summary: Fans turned out in large numbers to celebrate the Golden State Valkyries' championship, with ridership surprising SFMTA and BART.

items.title: AI stocks rebound after $2.5 trillion selloff
items.summary: AI and tech shares rose after losing roughly $2.5 trillion in market value, a selloff driven partly by concerns that Democratic election wins would slow AI development. Investors are bracing for further volatility.

items.title: Chainalysis says hackers stole credentials and tokens for all of its customers
items.summary: The blockchain analytics firm said a multifront cyberattack, which included AI agents and an on-path interception of data, exposed credentials and tokens for its entire customer base.

items.title: Oakland Coliseum and Arena to lay off more than 1,600 workers
items.summary: The venues will lay off their entire staff. At least two affected unions say they are negotiating to continue working under new ownership.

items.title: Israel's Arab-led parties could decide outcome of inconclusive election
items.summary: Israel's center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but would need backing from Arab-led parties.

items.title: How San Francisco neighborhoods voted on reopening the Great Highway
items.summary: A breakdown of results by neighborhood shows how each part of San Francisco voted on the Great Highway reopening measure.

items.title: Essay argues AI is significantly accelerating AI research
items.summary: A widely discussed piece argues that AI tools are dramatically speeding up the pace of AI research.

items.title: Google acquires Crusoe's data center site in southeast Wyoming
items.summary: Google has bought a data center site in southeast Wyoming previously held by Crusoe.

items.title: Distant polling places and unreliable mail hinder Native American voters in California
items.summary: Advocates say access barriers persist for Native American voters, and the state panel created to address them has never met.

items.title: $11.4 million in Nvidia hardware vanished in transit from Oakland to Texas
items.summary: Six pallets of Nvidia hardware disappeared en route to Texas; there have been no arrests two months later.

items.title: Developer ends Roku screensaver deal after Fox acquisition
items.summary: A developer ended a lucrative screensaver arrangement with Roku because Fox bought the company.

items.title: Newsom commutes death sentences for all 548 people on California's death row
items.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom said he will convert every death sentence to life without parole. California has historically had the largest death row population in the US.

items.title: Payment-skimming campaign targets restaurant delivery sites
items.summary: Researchers documented a campaign skimming payment card data from restaurant online ordering and delivery platforms.

items.title: Pope Leo begins 12-day South America tour weeks after lung cancer surgery
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV, who had part of a lung removed last month, started a three-nation trip in Uruguay and will also visit Argentina and Peru, where he spent two decades.

items.title: FAA to phase out floppy disks from air traffic control systems by 2028
items.summary: The FAA says its information display systems will be floppy-free at 435 sites by the end of 2028 in what it calls a historic upgrade.

items.title: Health security group issues warning after cyberattack on French blood bank
items.summary: A healthcare intelligence-sharing organization urged members to lock down systems after cyberattacks on cold storage systems, including at a French blood bank.

items.title: Women at Chowchilla prison reported abuse before 'Operation Breakdown'
items.summary: Former correctional officer Gregory Rodriguez was charged in 2022 with sexually assaulting thirteen women at the Central California Women's Facility; KQED examines the events that followed.

items.title: Satellite company moves into building rockets amid tight launch market
items.summary: A satellite maker is developing its own Blacklift rocket, citing a constrained launch market and a chance to expand its business.

items.title: European prosecutors probe EU rail funds after Spain's Urda train disaster
items.summary: Investigators are examining EU funds meant to upgrade the Spanish rail line where a crash killed 69 people.

items.title: Meta drops terms change that would have required AI training on Facebook page content
items.summary: Meta abandoned a commercial terms update that would have forced Facebook page owners to allow AI training on linked content.

items.title: Final weekend of Highway 101 lane closures in San Francisco
items.summary: Caltrans lane closures on Highway 101 in San Francisco enter their final weekend.

items.title: Oakland's First Fridays canceled for November
items.summary: Oakland's monthly First Fridays street event will not take place in November.

items.title: Wisconsin reports measles death of a baby, first such death in over 35 years
items.summary: A baby has died of measles in Wisconsin. Experts will determine next week whether the US has lost its measles elimination status.

items.title: Dozens of Democrats considering 2028 presidential bids, says former Obama aide
items.summary: Jim Messina told the BBC he has spoken with more than two dozen potential campaigns since the midterms, some of which are already hiring staff.

items.title: Hubble image of globular cluster M30 released
items.summary: A new NASA/ESA Hubble image shows the star cluster Messier 30 (NGC 7099), which offers insight into galactic history.

items.title: Quantum theorem undermines Einstein's view of reality
items.summary: Research building on efforts to defend Einstein's classical notion of reality has instead produced results that further challenge it.

items.title: Two killed in bus crash in France
items.summary: A child and a young adult died and others were injured in a bus crash, French authorities said.

items.title: Judge blocks construction of Trump's 250-foot arch
items.summary: A federal judge halted the project moments after it received federal agency approval; the administration had hoped to begin construction this week.

items.title: New wave of bomb threats targets European flights and broadcasters
items.summary: Officials across Europe reported further hoax bomb threats against flights following diversions earlier in the week, and three broadcasters were also threatened. No explosives have been found; a Russian extremist group denied involvement.

items.title: Asian supermarket opens in long-vacant San Francisco space
items.summary: A new Asian supermarket has opened in a San Francisco storefront that had been empty for years.

items.title: Tanzanian opposition leader convicted of inciting unrest, acquitted of treason
items.summary: The 58-year-old opposition leader, detained since April last year, says the charges are politically motivated.

items.title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie sentenced for murders of 191 people
items.summary: Mackenzie was convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult after ordering followers to starve themselves and their children to 'meet Jesus'. NPR reported a 200-year sentence; the BBC reported a life sentence.

items.title: Congress summons Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over Chinese espionage concerns
items.summary: Lawmakers are seeking answers about Huang's ties to an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.

items.title: Trinidad and Tobago to seek Cabinet approval for refinery restart process
items.summary: The government plans to seek Cabinet approval to begin a process for restarting the country's refinery.

items.title: White-collar workers quit jobs fearing AI disruption
items.summary: Some white-collar workers are leaving their jobs over concerns that AI will disrupt their fields.

items.title: Former lawmaker sentenced to 12.5 years in Macao's first national security case
items.summary: Au's arrest last year was the first publicly known prosecution under Macao's national security law since it was enacted in 2009.

items.title: Microsoft buyout offer unsettles its workforce
items.summary: Microsoft has offered buyouts to employees, creating uncertainty among its staff.

items.title: San Francisco public bank measure pulls ahead
items.summary: Proposition B, which would begin the process of creating a city-owned bank, has gained support with each update from elections officials.

items.title: Traces of blood found in 115-million-year-old dinosaur bones
items.summary: Scientists chemically confirmed remnants of ancient blood in dinosaur bones, challenging assumptions about how long biological molecules can survive.

items.title: Ghana and Trinidad and Tobago discuss joint approach to reparatory justice
items.summary: Ghana and Trinidad and Tobago held talks on reparatory justice and bilateral cooperation, including exploring a joint mechanism to pursue reparations.

items.title: UAE makes major AI investment as Sam Altman unveils energy plan
items.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced a large AI investment as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman presented a plan to transform the energy industry.

items.title: Humanoid robot cleaning service launches in San Francisco
items.summary: An MIT Technology Review reporter tested a new humanoid-robot house cleaning service operating in San Francisco.

items.title: Five-inch beetle larvae identified as cause of blueberry root damage
items.summary: Researchers identified the beetle species whose large larvae have been destroying blueberry roots in North Carolina for more than a decade.

items.title: November sky features meteor showers, a supermoon and Mars-Jupiter pairing
items.summary: November brings meteor fireballs, a close pairing of Mars and Jupiter and a supermoon, while Voyager 1 becomes the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth.

items.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension
items.summary: The ruling deepens a political crisis and casts doubt on the timetable for next year's elections, which would be the first nationwide vote since 1969.

items.title: Satellite images show major construction near Iranian missile bases
items.summary: Imagery from November shows digging and new buildings near Iranian missile sites.

items.title: NASA's Swift observatory re-enters atmosphere after nearly 22 years
items.summary: Swift, designed for a two-year mission, re-entered over Indonesia after nearly 22 years studying gamma-ray bursts, black holes and other high-energy events.

items.title: Satellite view of Utah's Goosenecks meanders
items.summary: NASA imagery shows the deep, tightly curving meanders carved by the San Juan River in the Utah desert.

items.title: AI stock selloff raises questions about Utah's data center plans
items.summary: The post-midterm selloff in AI stocks has prompted questions about the future of planned data center projects in Utah.

items.title: Man detained after shooting near Muni bus in North Beach
items.summary: San Francisco police detained a man after a shooting near a Muni bus in North Beach.

items.title: California Democrats flip five House seats and eye a sixth
items.summary: Aided by redistricting and voter disapproval of President Trump, Democrats won five Republican-held House seats in California, with another seat projected as safely Republican still in play.

items.title: Low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in people with Alzheimer's risk gene
items.summary: Four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in healthy middle-aged adults carrying the high-risk APOE4 gene, a study found.

items.title: AI data centers struggle to find space in San Francisco
items.summary: Companies seeking to build AI data centers in San Francisco face a shortage of suitable locations.

items.title: Top Democrats call for national data center moratorium after midterm sweep
items.summary: Leading Democrats are calling to rein in the AI infrastructure buildout following their midterm victories, including a national moratorium on data centers.

items.title: Paraguay's president impeached minutes after resigning over bank collapse
items.summary: Lawmakers voted to impeach Santiago Peña after his resignation, following the collapse of a digital bank tied to his government that froze millions of people's savings.

items.title: Russell Brand to be sentenced Monday after rape and sexual assault convictions
items.summary: A London jury found Brand guilty of multiple counts of sexual assault and one count of rape; the judge has warned the sentence will likely be significant.

items.title: Space station photo shows city lights from the Midwest to the East Coast
items.summary: An image taken from the ISS on Oct. 18 shows Chicago, Detroit and the New York metropolitan area before sunrise.

items.title: Self-forming membrane separates crude oil at room temperature
items.summary: Researchers developed a membrane that uses the oil itself to form filtration channels, which they say could cut refining energy use by about 32% and carbon emissions by about 38%.

items.title: Senate to vote on bill to speed US energy infrastructure buildout
items.summary: The Senate is set to vote in November on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which aims to cut permitting red tape for energy infrastructure.

items.title: Enceladus seen in silhouette
items.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day for November 5 shows Saturn's moon Enceladus in silhouette.

items.title: Cyprus exposes an ancient piece of ocean floor
items.summary: NASA imagery highlights Cyprus, the Mediterranean's third-largest island, where ophiolites expose ancient oceanic crust.

items.title: NASA unveils X-70 experimental research aircraft
items.summary: NASA introduced the X-70 Fractal at Kennedy Space Center, a configurable platform intended to speed development and testing of advanced aviation technologies.

items.title: Texas Democratic wins cast doubt on state's AI data center boom
items.summary: Texas, the fastest-growing US data center market, elected Democrat James Talarico to the Senate over Ken Paxton and Gina Hinojosa as governor, which may threaten its position in Big Tech's AI buildout.

items.title: US energy policy outlook after Democrats win both chambers of Congress
items.summary: Democrats took control of both the House and Senate in the midterms, a shift with implications for US energy policy.

items.title: Researchers test whether AI models can report their own internal states
items.summary: By injecting 'thoughts' directly into large language models, researchers are mapping the extent of AI models' capacity for introspection.

items.title: Brain's cross-wiring may trace back to vision in ancient fish
items.summary: Scientists propose that the brain's contralateral wiring originated over 500 million years ago in the visual systems of early fish.

items.title: Study finds permanent daylight saving time would add billions of dark school commutes
items.summary: Researchers estimate permanent DST would mean at least 2 billion more US school commutes in darkness, with potential safety and circadian effects.

items.title: MIT team uses flexible linkers to create new nanoparticle crystal structures
items.summary: MIT scientists found that flexible rather than rigid molecular connections can produce previously unseen nanoparticle arrangements.

items.title: NASA weighs plan to save Hubble from re-entry
items.summary: With Hubble slowly losing altitude after more than 35 years in orbit, NASA is exploring options to prevent its eventual fall to Earth.

items.title: SLAC researchers confirm altermagnetism as a third type of magnetism
items.summary: Using specialized X-ray techniques, scientists observed a magnetic signature confirming altermagnetism as distinct from ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism.

items.title: AI helps Stanford researchers find natural appetite-suppressing molecule
items.summary: A molecule called BRP suppressed appetite and promoted fat loss in animals without the digestive side effects or significant muscle loss associated with Ozempic.

items.title: Trinidad and Tobago breaks with longstanding ICC support in UN vote
items.summary: Trinidad and Tobago departed from its longstanding support for the International Criminal Court in a United Nations vote.

items.title: Hidden companion star may be disturbing Betelgeuse's atmosphere
items.summary: Radio observations suggest a companion star named Siwarha is moving through Betelgeuse's extended atmosphere and causing disturbances.

items.title: Akrotiri, Greece's 'Pompeii', was buried by Thera eruption
items.summary: The Bronze Age town of Akrotiri on Santorini was buried in volcanic ash by the Thera eruption in the 17th–16th century BCE.
